name: (CS)²AI Online™ Seminar: Cybersecurity Vulnerability Reporting & Remediation
description:
Last year Billy and his team hacked a connected wheelchair and sent it careening down a flight of stairs.

Recently the manufacturer issued a patch to its customers that addresses the authentication and encryption weaknesses we exploited. The update has received 510(k) clearance from the FDA, and the patch is cleared for installation on devices. Thus, the circle is complete, the bugs are no more, and the issues we found have been mitigated. The time between public notification and patch release to the public was about 90 days. These 90 days include coordination for public notification, firmware development work, firmware testing, and the FDA’s 510(k) process.

For those interested in the behind-the-scenes process of vulnerability discovery, reporting and remediation, how it was built and operates, this talk is for you. Register now to learn more about one of the most mature cybersecurity regulatory frameworks in the world.

# ☕ The OG Coffee&Code Meetup

### A Blockspace Community × Coffee&Code Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”
This is **The OG Coffee&Code**—the meetup that started it all, now presented in collaboration with the **Blockspace Community**.
No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

## What this meetup is

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

## What this meetup is not

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

## How it works

1. Show up
2. Grab coffee ☕
3. Open your laptop, notebook, or sketchpad
4. Work at your own pace
5. Chat when you want and focus when you need
6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

## Who should attend

* Software engineers and data professionals
* Students and self-learners
* Founders and indie hackers
* Designers, tinkerers, and technologists
* Members of the Blockspace and Coffee&Code communities
* Anyone who enjoys building things with other humans

Whether this is your first Coffee&Code, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.
This collaboration brings together two communities around a shared goal: creating a relaxed, supportive space where people can build, learn, and connect.

**Come for the code.**
**Stay for the community.**
**Leave caffeinated. ☕🚀**

name: 15th Philly Hardware Meetup @ Drexel!
description:
Join us for the 15th Philadelphia Hardware Meetup! Come join us to hear from our guest speakers as well as share what’s on your desk. We always have time for an open mic.

***[Please click here to RSVP on Luma!](https://luma.com/knl1e93t)***

​​​This time, we're at **Drexel University's Bossone Research Enterprise Center**. This is our first time collaborating with a university as a venue and we're really excited to connect more students to professionals!

​*Hardware Meetups happen across 30+ cities monthly and help bring together different professionals to connect and meet each other.*

​**We will have a great set of featured speakers for the evening!:**

* **[Glennon Simmons](https://www.linkedin.com/in/glennonsimmons/)** is co-founder and CEO of **[Portable Diagnostic Systems](http://portabledx.com/)** (PDS), a biotech company developing portable, lab-quality diagnostic technology for use outside traditional laboratories. An inventor and entrepreneur with nearly two decades of experience in microfluidics and point-of-care diagnostics, Glennon previously led research and development of lab-on-a-chip technologies at New York University. Building on that work, he founded PDS to address critical gaps in rapid drug detection and forensic toxicology. The company's Integrity-1 Analysis System combines microfluidics, biosensing, machine vision, and AI to detect multiple drugs from small fluid samples in minutes, bringing sophisticated testing capabilities directly to clinicians, investigators, and first responders.
* **[Matt Starfield](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mattstarfield/)**, Senior EE at **[Solid Product Design](http://solidpd.com/)** and advisor at **[NextFab Ventures](https://nextfabventures.com/)**. He earned his MS-EE from Drexel University in 2007, where he did his graduate research in the Drexel Wireless Systems Lab under Dr. Kapil Dandekar. Since then, Matt has spent more than a decade helping hardware startups go from idea, to prototype, to product. Today, he develops advanced agentic AI systems that apply that same rigor and discipline, autonomously. Matt shares the origin story, methods, guardrails, and bench-proven results from a year of building advanced AI systems into his daily hardware engineering work. Expect a clear preview of where agentic hardware development is going next.
* **[Chris Chong](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chrischongdesign/)**, co-founder and the Chief Design Officer at **[Mexar](http://mexar.co/)**, a climate adaptation startup which launched their first product, the Vapor, this Summer. Chris is joining us to talk about the development and manufacturing process behind the Vapor.

​**Thank you to our partners!:**

**[Efinix](https://www.efinixinc.com/index.html?utm_source=luma)** manufactures the world’s most efficient FPGAs. Delivering low power, high performance and small physical size, Efinix FPGAs offer fast time to market in a cost-effective footprint. Efinix offers three families of FPGAs from the entry level Trion family that prioritizes I/O and connectivity to the Titanium family that offer high speed transceivers and high compute capability for industrial, edge and highly accelerated AI applications. The portfolio spans 4,000 logic elements up 375,000 logic elements and includes SiP offering with Flash and system memory in the same FPGA package. These highly integrated solutions reduce design complexity, increase available I/O and further speed time to market. The Efinix Efinity tool suite is freely available and delivers an intuitive RTL to bit-stream capability while supporting a rich IP library and software compilers for the suite of Sapphire RISC-V processors available as both hard IP and soft macros across the Efinix portfolio.
Efinix FPGAs have been widely adopted in a broad array of markets from industrial automation , communications, medical, automotive and test and measurement. To find out more about Efinix products and markets, visit [www.efinixinc.com](http://www.efinixinc.com/ "http://www.efinixinc.com").

​[Ben Franklin Technology Partners](https://benfranklin.org/?utm_source=luma), our food sponsor for the evening. BFTP creates and retains highly paid, sustainable jobs by investing in and linking early-stage technology firms and established manufacturers with experts, universities, follow-on funding, and other resources to help them prosper through innovation.

description:
## **Join Philadelphia's leading community for AI, SaaS & Technology growth.**

Please register here: https://luma.com/wbaeeeaw

​Our mission is to build the #1 community for founders, operators, executives, investors, and builders growing AI-first SaaS, technology, and innovation-driven companies, through real relationships, shared learning, and growth-focused collaboration.
​Every Meetup delivers intentional networking, actionable insights, and direct access to leaders who know what it takes to grow, fund, scale, and exit in today's competitive market.
​If you're serious about building in AI, SaaS, or Tech, this is where you belong.

​**Healthcare AI: Product Development from Concept to Launch**
​Healthcare is one of the hardest places to ship AI: a product has to fit real clinical workflows and earn the trust of the people using it. Chris Cera will walk through how a healthcare idea becomes a validated, launch-ready product, including where AI solves a real problem and how to pressure-test an idea before investing heavily.
​Whether you're validating a healthcare idea, adding AI to an existing product, or evaluating digital health as an investor, you'll leave with practical ideas you can apply to your business.

​About the Speaker
​**Chris Cera, CEO, Arcweb Technologies**
​Chris leads Arcweb Technologies, a Philadelphia-based Certified B Corp and AI product studio that has helped more than 100 organizations build digital health products. He previously co-founded Vuzit (acquired by Accusoft) and Philly Startup Leaders, and holds B.S. and M.S. degrees in Computer Science from Drexel University.

**REGISTER HERE: [https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)**

In recent months, AI has fundamentally reshaped cybersecurity. Automated tooling now discovers open-source vulnerabilities and generates exploits at unprecedented speeds. As the sheer volume and velocity of CVE disclosures overwhelm traditional workflows, IT and security teams face a daunting challenge: How do you patch rapidly without destabilizing mission-critical production environments?
Join us for the next [Philadelphia Red Hat User Group (RHUG)](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451) to explore how Red Hat turns the tide on AI-driven threats by securing the software supply chain from code to deployment.
What we'll cover:

* Red Hat Trusted Libraries: How cryptographically signed, SLSA-compliant binaries neutralize upstream risks before code hits production.
* Project Lightwell: How automated, validated patching and backports maintain enterprise stability in an AI-accelerated threat landscape.
* Peer Networking: Connect with local IT leaders and Red Hat experts over food and drinks at Philly's newest high-energy venue.

[Event Details:](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)

description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.
